generatedFrom.name: adhan
generatedFrom.readmeDescriptionSource: README.md carries no per-method prose. Each method description below is verbatim from METHODS.md, which README.md links as "Calculation Parameters & Methods Guide".

constructorSignature: new CalculationParameters(method, fajrAngle = 0, ishaAngle = 0, ishaInterval = 0, maghribAngle = 0)

invariantsAcrossAllMethods.madhab: Every one of the 13 factories leaves madhab at the class default Madhab.Shafi. No preset sets Hanafi. Asr follows the caller's assignment only.
invariantsAcrossAllMethods.highLatitudeRule: Every one of the 13 factories leaves highLatitudeRule at the class default HighLatitudeRule.MiddleOfTheNight. No preset selects SeventhOfTheNight, and HighLatitudeRule.recommended() is never called internally.
invariantsAcrossAllMethods.polarCircleResolution: Every preset leaves the class default PolarCircleResolution.Unresolved.
invariantsAcrossAllMethods.shafaq: Every preset leaves the class default Shafaq.General.
invariantsAcrossAllMethods.adjustments: User adjustments start at all-zero and are per-prayer minutes, added to methodAdjustments.
invariantsAcrossAllMethods.rounding: Nearest for 12 of 13. Singapore sets Up. Nothing sets None.
invariantsAcrossAllMethods.nightPortions: Derived only from highLatitudeRule and, for TwilightAngle, from the instance's fajrAngle/ishaAngle. It is not a per-method table.
invariantsAcrossAllMethods.methodField: params.method is load-bearing. PrayerTimes compares it against the literal string 'MoonsightingCommittee' to switch Fajr and Isha onto the season-adjusted twilight curve and the 1/7 rule above latitude 55. A null method is coerced to 'Other' in the constructor.

dateComponents.howTaken: SolarTime calls Astronomical.julianDay(date.getFullYear(), date.getMonth() + 1, date.getDate(), 0). PrayerTimes then rebuilds every result with TimeComponents.utcDate(date.getFullYear(), date.getMonth(), date.getDate()). Both read the LOCAL calendar components of the Date argument and both use those components to build a UTC instant.
dateComponents.therefore: The Date argument is a calendar-day selector, not an instant. Its year, month and day are read in the host time zone; hour, minute, second and millisecond are discarded. The six returned values are absolute UTC instants for that Gregorian day at that longitude.
dateComponents.hazard: A Date built from a UTC epoch (for example Date.parse('2026-06-01')) reads as the previous day on any host west of UTC. Construct the day in the calculation's own local terms, or build it at local noon.
dateComponents.daylightSaving: No DST logic exists in the library. README.md states the returned Date instances are absolute UTC values and instructs callers to format them against an explicit IANA zone such as Europe/London. MIGRATION.md records that 4.0.0 removed adhan.Date.formattedTime for this reason.
dateComponents.polarScope: When the polar resolver fires it recomputes transit, sunrise and sunset from the resolved SolarTime but keeps the original date components, so the returned day does not shift.

roundingModes.implementation: DateUtils.roundedMinute(date, rounding) reads date.getUTCSeconds() and adds a signed second offset, so rounding happens on the absolute instant in UTC seconds.
roundingModes.nearest: Default. seconds >= 30 adds (60 - seconds), otherwise subtracts seconds. Floor at :00 to :29, ceiling at :30 to :59.
roundingModes.up: Always adds (60 - seconds). A value already exactly on the minute gains a whole minute, because 60 - 0 = 60. Up is therefore not idempotent at :00.
roundingModes.none: Offset 0. Seconds are left as computed, so the stored Date carries sub-minute precision.
roundingModes.appliedTo: All six outputs including sunset. Sunset is the only output with no adjustment applied, yet it is still rounded.
roundingModes.order: Per prayer: raw astronomical time -> add adjustments -> add methodAdjustments -> roundedMinute. Rounding is last and never re-enters the calculation.
roundingModes.sunnahException: SunnahTimes calls roundedMinute with no rounding argument, so middleOfTheNight and lastThirdOfTheNight always round Nearest regardless of params.rounding.

ishaIntervalInteraction.trigger: if (calculationParameters.ishaInterval > 0) takes the interval branch; otherwise the angle branch runs.
ishaIntervalInteraction.base: isha = sunsetTime + ishaInterval minutes, measured from the raw unadjusted sunsetTime. It is not measured from the rounded maghrib and not from sunset plus maghribAdjustment.
ishaIntervalInteraction.adjustmentsStillApply: ishaAdjustment (user plus method) is added after the interval is applied, then the result is rounded. A maghrib adjustment does not move an interval-based Isha.
ishaIntervalInteraction.highLatitudeSuppressed: The entire night-clamp block (nightPortions, seasonAdjustedEveningTwilight, the MoonsightingCommittee 55-degree 1/7 override) sits in the else branch. An interval-based Isha receives no high-latitude bound and no semantic guarantee that it precedes Fajr.
ishaIntervalInteraction.nightPortionsSuppressed: nightPortions().isha is never consulted when ishaInterval > 0. Under TwilightAngle the Isha portion equals ishaAngle / 60, which is 0 for UmmAlQura and Qatar, so setting ishaInterval back to 0 on those presets leaves Isha on the 0-degree crossing rather than on sunset.
ishaIntervalInteraction.maghribAngleOrder: The maghribAngle test runs after Isha is computed, so it can see the interval result.

highLatitudeMechanics.nightDefinition: night = (tomorrowSunrise - todaySunset) in seconds, with tomorrowSunrise taken from a full SolarTime built at date + 1 day. It is the same night length for both ends.
highLatitudeMechanics.fajrClamp: safeFajr = sunrise - portion * night. Fajr becomes safeFajr when the angle result is NaN or when safeFajr is later than the angle result. Fajr can only be pushed later.
highLatitudeMechanics.ishaClamp: safeIsha = sunset + portion * night. Isha becomes safeIsha when the angle result is NaN or when safeIsha is earlier than the angle result. Isha can only be pulled earlier.
highLatitudeMechanics.portions: MiddleOfTheNight gives fajr 1/2 and isha 1/2. SeventhOfTheNight gives 1/7 and 1/7. TwilightAngle gives fajrAngle/60 and ishaAngle/60, an angle-derived fraction of the night, so the clamp moves with the method's angles.
highLatitudeMechanics.notAutomatic: No latitude threshold triggers a rule change. Line 48 of METHODS.md recommends SeventhOfTheNight above 48 degrees; HighLatitudeRule.recommended() encodes exactly that latitude > 48 test. The caller must invoke it.

clampDirection.oneWayOnly: Both clamps are one-way comparisons, not assignments. Fajr is replaced only when the clamped value is LATER than the astronomical one; Isha only when it is EARLIER. A clamp can therefore never rescue a time that started on the wrong side of sunrise or sunset. CalculationMethod.Other() in its delivered state is the proof: fajr lands about 7 minutes after sunrise and isha about 6 minutes before sunset, and the MiddleOfTheNight clamp stays silent.
clampDirection.zeroAngleIsNotHorizon: Sunrise and sunset use a target altitude of -50/60 degrees, the standard refraction and semidiameter correction, hard-coded as solarAltitude in SolarTime. Prayer angles are used raw, so 0 degrees means the sun's centre geometrically on the horizon, later in the morning and earlier in the evening than the sunrise and sunset convention.
clampDirection.londonMidsummerCollapse: At 51.5074 N on 2026-06-01 the MiddleOfTheNight clamp sets both ends for the 18-degree and deeper pairs. Muslim World League, Egyptian, Karachi, Kuwait, Turkey and Dubai return Fajr 00:59 and Isha 00:58, one minute apart across midnight, because the true twilights do not occur. Singapore lands on the same instants and its Rounding.Up pushes them to 01:00 and 00:59. The 15-degree ISNA pair stays inside the day at 02:05 and 23:54, and the MoonsightingCommittee curve at 02:56 and 22:22, because a shallower angle is reached before the half-night limit. Only those two and the interval methods keep a workable day at that latitude and season.

moonsightingSpecialCase.gate: calculationParameters.method === 'MoonsightingCommittee' && coordinates.latitude >= 55. Constant HIGH_LATITUDE_THRESHOLD = 55 in PrayerTimes.js. North of that line the 1/7 night fraction replaces the 18-degree result before the season-adjusted value is considered.
moonsightingSpecialCase.fajr: Overridden to sunrise - night/7, then raised to seasonAdjustedMorningTwilight if that is later.
moonsightingSpecialCase.isha: Overridden to sunset + night/7, then lowered to seasonAdjustedEveningTwilight if that is earlier.
moonsightingSpecialCase.twilightCurve: Astronomical.seasonAdjustedMorningTwilight and seasonAdjustedEveningTwilight are latitude- and day-of-year-driven polynomial interpolations anchored on the solstice. They are independent of fajrAngle and ishaAngle. Evening twilight depends on shafaq: General, Ahmer or Abyad pick different coefficient sets.
moonsightingSpecialCase.consequence: For this method the configured 18-degree angles act only as the pre-clamp value below 55 degrees and as a comparison term above it. Editing them changes almost nothing.

maghribAngleMechanics.onlyTehran: Tehran is the sole preset with maghribAngle > 0 (4.5 degrees).
maghribAngleMechanics.acceptanceTest: The angle-based Maghrib is adopted only when sunsetTime < angleBasedMaghrib AND ishaTime > angleBasedMaghrib. Outside that window Maghrib stays at sunset.
maghribAngleMechanics.selfGating: The guard makes the angle harmless when it would land after Isha, so it cannot produce Maghrib later than Isha on a normal day.

polarCircle.trigger: Fires when the resolver is not Unresolved and today's sunrise or sunset is invalid, or tomorrow's sunrise is NaN.
polarCircle.default: Unresolved leaves the invalid Date in place. Downstream code that formats an Invalid Date gets NaN, not an error.
polarCircle.strategies: AqrabYaum walks dates forward and back up to 183 days. AqrabBalad walks latitude toward the equator in 0.5-degree steps, ignoring the equatorward limit below 65 degrees.

sunnahTimes.nightDefinition: nightDuration = nextDayPrayerTimes.fajr - this.maghrib, both taken from the already-rounded PrayerTimes objects, so rounding error compounds across the day boundary.
sunnahTimes.outputs: middleOfTheNight = maghrib + nightDuration/2. lastThirdOfTheNight = maghrib + nightDuration * 2/3.

qibla.implementation: Fixed Kaaba coordinates 21.4225241 N, 39.8261818 E. atan2 spherical bearing, unwound to 0 to 360. No runtime input beyond the observer coordinates.

methods.name: MuslimWorldLeague
methods.fajrRule: Sun 18 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 17 degrees below the horizon after sunset (angle, not interval).
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2 of the night (sunset to next sunrise). Angle-derived if the caller switches to TwilightAngle: 18/60 and 17/60.
methods.readmeDescription: Muslim World League. Standard Fajr time with an angle of 18 degrees. Earlier Isha time with an angle of 17 degrees.

methods.name: Egyptian
methods.fajrRule: Sun 19.5 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 17.5 degrees below the horizon after sunset.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. TwilightAngle would give 19.5/60 and 17.5/60.
methods.readmeDescription: Egyptian General Authority of Survey. Early Fajr time using an angle 19.5 degrees and a slightly earlier Isha time using an angle of 17.5 degrees.

methods.name: Karachi
methods.fajrRule: Sun 18 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 18 degrees below the horizon after sunset.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. TwilightAngle would give 18/60 and 18/60.
methods.readmeDescription: University of Islamic Sciences, Karachi. A generally applicable method that uses standard Fajr and Isha angles of 18 degrees.

methods.name: UmmAlQura
methods.fajrRule: Sun 18.5 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Interval: raw sunset plus 90 minutes. ishaAngle is 0 and unused.
methods.nightPortions: Configured as fajr 1/2, isha 1/2, but the Isha portion is never read because ishaInterval is 90. Fajr still clamps at 1/2 the night.
methods.specialBehavior: No Ramadan branch exists. METHODS.md tells the caller to add a +30 minute custom adjustment to Isha during Ramadan; the 90-minute interval is otherwise fixed. At London in June the 90-minute interval keeps Isha at 22:38 while every angle-based method is clamped past midnight, so this preset is the only one that stays sane there.
methods.readmeDescription: Umm al-Qura University, Makkah. Uses a fixed interval of 90 minutes from maghrib to calculate Isha. And a slightly earlier Fajr time with an angle of 18.5 degrees. Note: you should add a +30 minute custom adjustment for Isha during Ramadan.

methods.name: Dubai
methods.fajrRule: Sun 18.2 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 18.2 degrees below the horizon after sunset.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. TwilightAngle would give 18.2/60 at both ends.
methods.specialBehavior: Four method adjustments, including a negative sunrise shift of -3 minutes. Maghrib moves +3 minutes but is measured from sunset, not from the shifted sunrise.
methods.readmeDescription: Used in the UAE. Slightly earlier Fajr time and slightly later Isha time with angles of 18.2 degrees for Fajr and Isha in addition to 3 minute offsets for sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, and Maghrib.

methods.name: MoonsightingCommittee
methods.fajrRule: Below 55 degrees latitude, sun 18 degrees below the horizon, then raised to the season-adjusted morning twilight if that is later. At or above 55 degrees, sunrise minus one seventh of the night, then raised to the season-adjusted morning twilight if that is later.
methods.ishaRule: Below 55 degrees, sun 18 degrees below the horizon, then lowered to the season-adjusted evening twilight if that is earlier. At or above 55 degrees, sunset plus one seventh of the night, then lowered to the season-adjusted evening twilight if that is earlier.
methods.nightPortions: Nominally fajr 1/2 and isha 1/2, but this method bypasses nightPortions entirely and uses the season-adjusted twilight polynomial. highLatitudeRule therefore has no effect on its Fajr and Isha.
methods.specialBehavior: The only method with a named branch in PrayerTimes.js. HIGH_LATITUDE_THRESHOLD = 55 switches in the 1/7 night rule. shafaq selects the evening twilight coefficient set (Ahmer earlier, Abyad later). Recognised by string comparison on params.method, so copying its parameters onto another method name silently disables all of this.
methods.readmeDescription: Method developed by Khalid Shaukat, founder of Moonsighting Committee Worldwide. Uses standard 18 degree angles for Fajr and Isha in addition to seasonal adjustment values. This method automatically applies the 1/7 approximation rule for locations at or above 55 degrees latitude. Recommended for North America and the UK.

methods.name: NorthAmerica
methods.fajrRule: Sun 15 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 15 degrees below the horizon after sunset.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. TwilightAngle would give 15/60 at both ends.
methods.specialBehavior: The 15-degree pair is the most sensitive to the MiddleOfTheNight clamp, because such a low Isha angle frequently falls past midnight at UK summer latitudes.
methods.readmeDescription: Also known as the ISNA method. Can be used for North America, but the moonsightingCommittee method is preferable. Gives later Fajr times and early Isha times with angles of 15 degrees.

methods.name: Kuwait
methods.fajrRule: Sun 18 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 17.5 degrees below the horizon after sunset.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. TwilightAngle would give 18/60 and 17.5/60.
methods.specialBehavior: No adjustments at all, so its output is the raw astronomical result plus rounding.
methods.readmeDescription: Standard Fajr time with an angle of 18 degrees. Slightly earlier Isha time with an angle of 17.5 degrees.

methods.name: Qatar
methods.fajrRule: Sun 18 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Interval: raw sunset plus 90 minutes. ishaAngle is 0 and unused.
methods.nightPortions: Configured as fajr 1/2, isha 1/2, but the Isha portion is never read because ishaInterval is 90.
methods.specialBehavior: Shares UmmAlQura's 90-minute interval with an 18-degree Fajr instead of 18.5. No Ramadan handling.
methods.readmeDescription: Same Isha interval as ummAlQura but with the standard Fajr time using an angle of 18 degrees.

methods.name: Singapore
methods.fajrRule: Sun 20 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 18 degrees below the horizon after sunset.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. TwilightAngle would give 20/60 and 18/60.
methods.specialBehavior: The only preset that changes rounding, to Rounding.Up, so every time including sunset advances to the next whole minute and an exact :00 gains a further minute.
methods.readmeDescription: Used in Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Early Fajr time with an angle of 20 degrees and standard Isha time with an angle of 18 degrees.

methods.name: Tehran
methods.fajrRule: Sun 17.7 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 14 degrees below the horizon after sunset.
methods.maghribRule: Angle: sun 4.5 degrees below the horizon after sunset, adopted only when it falls after sunset and before Isha. Otherwise sunset.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. TwilightAngle would give 17.7/60 and 14/60, the smallest Isha portion of any preset.
methods.specialBehavior: The only method whose Maghrib is not sunset. Its maghribAngle sits in the fifth constructor slot, so a caller reconstructing the preset by hand must order the arguments exactly.
methods.readmeDescription: Institute of Geophysics, University of Tehran. Early Isha time with an angle of 14 degrees. Slightly later Fajr time with an angle of 17.7 degrees. Calculates Maghrib based on the sun reaching an angle of 4.5 degrees below the horizon.

methods.name: Turkey
methods.fajrRule: Sun 18 degrees below the horizon before sunrise.
methods.ishaRule: Sun 17 degrees below the horizon after sunset.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. TwilightAngle would give 18/60 and 17/60.
methods.specialBehavior: Four method adjustments with the largest spread in the package: sunrise -7, Dhuhr +5, Asr +4, Maghrib +7. Fajr and Isha carry none. METHODS.md calls the result an approximation of Diyanet.
methods.readmeDescription: An approximation of the Diyanet method used in Turkey. This approximation is less accurate outside the region of Turkey.

methods.name: Other
methods.fajrRule: No angle. A zero angle is not the horizon: fajrAngle 0 makes the target altitude 0 degrees, whose morning crossing sits about 7 minutes AFTER sunrise, and the MiddleOfTheNight clamp cannot correct it because that clamp only ever moves Fajr later.
methods.ishaRule: No angle and no interval. ishaAngle 0 gives the 0-degree evening crossing, about 6 minutes BEFORE sunset, and the night clamp cannot correct it because that clamp only ever moves Isha earlier.
methods.nightPortions: fajr 1/2, isha 1/2. Because both angles are 0, TwilightAngle would give a portion of 0 at both ends.
methods.specialBehavior: Blank template, and degenerate as delivered: Fajr falls after sunrise and Isha before sunset until the caller supplies angles. A null method passed to CalculationParameters is coerced to this name.
methods.readmeDescription: Defaults to angles of 0 degrees, should generally be used for making a custom method and setting your own values.

notInPackage: No Indonesia preset (Kemenag). Singapore's description claims Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore share one 20/18 preset.
No Nigeria preset (no Nigerian Supreme Council or Unity/NABIM variant).
No Malaysia preset (JAKIM). Only the Singapore preset's description mentions Malaysia.
No Kazakhstan preset (Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Kazakhstan).
No Morocco preset (Ministry of Habous and Islamic Affairs).
No Umm al-Qura Ramadan switch. The 120-minute Ramadan interval must be applied by the caller as a +30 minute Isha adjustment.
No per-method Madhab. Every preset is Shafi and Hanafi must be assigned by the caller.
No per-method HighLatitudeRule. Every preset is MiddleOfTheNight and the caller must assign SeventhOfTheNight, or call HighLatitudeRule.recommended().
No per-method polar circle strategy. Every preset is Unresolved.
No method registry by locale, country, city or timezone. Method selection is entirely the caller's.
No metadata on a method beyond the name string, the four angle/interval numbers, methodAdjustments and rounding.
No timezone data, no DST logic and no formatting helpers. adhan.Date.formattedTime was removed in 4.0.0.
No Hijri calendar, no Ramadan or Eid detection, no prayer-time tables and no caching.
No adhan or iqama audio, no notification logic, no per-prayer offsets beyond flat minutes, and no seasonal or monthly adjustment model.
No Indonesia/Malaysia 20-degree Isha variant, no Morocco 19/17 variant, no Kazakhstan 15/15 variant and no Nigeria 18/17 unity variant.
No API to read a method's provenance, source or scholarly reference. The only citations are METHODS.md prose and the Shared/Times fixture files, which ship outside the npm package.
